notes: Named Zosyn by Steven L. Shafer, 2026-11-18: "I prefer generic names, but for combination products that can be a problem. Call it Zosyn." A brand name is a valid R name, as MEGX and MDMA are, so it needs no display name. "The PK should be labelled piperacillin": the drug is Zosyn, its curve is labelled piperacillin, and tazobactam is not plotted. Earlier decision of the same day: tazobactam is not a drug of its own, being given only in combination; the products are listed as "Piperacillin/tazobactam" and "Ceftolozane/tazobactam", each dosed in the units of its FDA label. This row and the next replace the planned stand-alone tazobactam. No new paper: stanpumpR's piperacillin (Kong 2025, R/drugs_piperacillin.R) already takes a dose of the product and plots piperacillin, tazobactam not plotted. The change: list it as Piperacillin/tazobactam and dose it in the Zosyn label's units, g of the combined product for adults (2.25, 3.375 and 4.5 g; 3.375 g q6h is 13.5 g a day, 12.0 g piperacillin + 1.5 g tazobactam, 8:1) and mg/kg of the combined product for children (90 mg/kg from 2 to 9 months, 80 piperacillin + 10 tazobactam; 112.5 mg/kg over 9 months), in place of today's mg pip-tazo. Renaming the drug piperacillin to Zosyn leaves links naming piperacillin to be mapped to it. Zhang 2021 and Chandorkar 2015, the largest tazobactam fits in nlmixr2lib, are ceftolozane-tazobactam fits and belong to the next row.

Ceftolozane/tazobactam. Named Zerbaxa by Steven L. Shafer, 2026-11-18 ("Use Zerbaxa and Avycaz too", after naming Zosyn); its curve is labelled ceftolozane. The same decision of that day: dosed in the Zerbaxa label's units, g of the combined product for adults (1.5 g = 1 g ceftolozane + 0.5 g tazobactam, 2:1, q8h for cIAI and cUTI; 3 g for HABP/VABP) and mg/kg of the combined product for children (30 mg/kg = 20 ceftolozane + 10 tazobactam; 60 mg/kg; 75 mg/kg for HABP/VABP; each up to the adult dose). Plot ceftolozane, 2/3 of the dose, as piperacillin's product unit carries 4/4.5 (its doseProducts block); tazobactam not plotted. Source: Zhang 2021 (PMID 32949031, in the archive, read in full on the 2026-11-18 run for its tazobactam half), which fits both components; nlmixr2lib files its ceftolozane model as Zhang_2021_ceftolozane (968 participants). Label: DailyMed setid 70ac1d90-eff3-4f0b-9f46-5846c571b32f (May 2026). The model's volumes rise with the infection (pneumonia about doubles them). The open infection decision: decided 2026-11-18: an infection field, built in PR #861 (R/infection.R; categories none, cUTI, cIAI, pneumonia, pneumoniaVentilated, other; default none, Shafer 2026-11-24). Norvir. Kept as a drug of its own by Steven L. Shafer, 2026-11-23: "I would leave ritonavir in as a model, because the pharmacokinetics of CYP3A4 inhibition are interesting." Though given today almost only as a booster (Kaletra, Paxlovid, boosted darunavir and atazanavir), it is labelled alone. Its own disposition is nonlinear (it inhibits and induces its own CYP3A4 metabolism), which a source must describe. nlmixr2lib holds seven ritonavir models, all fitted in patients taking it as a booster (the largest Mensing 2017, 2,348 adults with hepatitis C on paritaprevir/ritonavir); whether a pick describes ritonavir's own time-dependent disposition is to be read.

Intravenous esketamine implemented 2026-11-25 from Sigtermans 2009 (PMID 19741495, read on the PDF), on Shafer's instruction of that day ('Implement esketamine from Sigtermans 2009'): three compartments per 70 kg linear in weight, CL1 75.1 L/h men and 97.3 women (R/drugs_esketamine.R). [decided] (Shafer, 2026-11-25: 'The peak effect of esketamine will be the same as for ketamine if it is given IV') tPeak 3 min, the library ketamine's, with ke0 solved from it; was ke0 3.78 /min from the 11 s t1/2 ke0 Sigtermans cite from Herd and Schuttler, which put the peak at 0.7 min. [decision] for Shafer: target-controlled infusion is not offered for esketamine, because the TCI API (docs/tci-api.md) refuses any target above 5 x a drug's upper typical concentration and esketamine has no band; a band (for example ketamine's 0.1-0.16 mcg/mL analgesic threshold scaled by potency, or Sigtermans' heat-pain C50 373 ng/mL) or an API rule for a drug without one would allow it. Nasal esketamine (Spravato) is not offered: Perez-Ruixo 2021 (PMID 33128208) needs a hepato-portal first-pass engine, per-device bioavailability and race terms, still the [decision] on its card. stanpumpR's ketamine is racemic. Weekly run 2026-11-24: the pick Perez-Ruixo 2021 (PMID 33128208, in the archive, read on the PDF) has a well-stirred hepato-portal compartment (Vh 101 L, Qh 151 L/h, Fgut 0.64 for oral and swallowed-nasal doses) that no engine carries. [decision] for Shafer: (a) an exact reduction or a new engine for that first pass; (b) nasal FRn falls from 0.54 for the first 28 mg to x0.62 per later 28-mg device, so per-dose-count bioavailability (doseDependent or oralSaturation as a stand-in?); (c) race terms (Asian on kel x0.36 and noresketamine CL/F x0.81, Japanese on FRn x1.34) with no Patient Profile race field: add one or apply none. Noresketamine would be metabolite-only. 2026-11-25: Shafer asked whether racemic ketamine's PK describe esketamine; on clearance they differ about 1.8-fold (library ketamine 13.2 mL/kg/min; esketamine alone 26.3 in Ihmsen 2001's crossover, 24.5-25.7 in Perez-Ruixo 2021), so the racemic model would overpredict esketamine (44% at steady state). [decision] on papers/digests/PMID_33128208.md recommends implementing esketamine from Ihmsen 2001's S(+) fit; Ihmsen 2001, Geisslinger 1993 and White 1985 requested (papers/pending-work.csv).

Simulect (chimeric anti-CD25 monoclonal antibody), IV, 20 mg on days 0 and 4 after transplantation; concentration only. Proposed by the transplant session 2026-11-25 and added on Shafer's yes the same day. Candidates, abstracts read in PubMed: Kovarik 1999, Transplantation 68:1288-94 (PMID 10573065; 169 adult kidney recipients on ciclosporin, empirical Bayes estimates CL 36.7 mL/h, V 8.0 L, half-life 7.4 days; weight and age each 6% or less of the variability); Kovarik 2001, Clin Pharmacol Ther 69:201-9 (PMID 11309548; 184 liver recipients, CL 55 mL/h, V 9.7 L, drained ascites raising clearance); Mentre 1999, J Pharmacokinet Biopharm 27:213-30 (PMID 10567956; the phase 2 population model behind the dose). The CD25-saturating concentration, 0.2 mcg/mL in kidney recipients, is a candidate threshold, not a therapeutic range. None is in the archive: the three full texts and the Simulect label are needed.
